claim: Evidence that Shell-style scenario planning improves outcomes is anecdotal and mixed; no controlled effect size on firm performance was obtained. Both supports are second-hand (Wikipedia, and Polyscene citing Cordova-Pozo and Rouwette 2023); Phelps 2001 and the 2020 black-box paper were never read.
agent_test: Do not assume the funnel helps; run it as an arm against plain and best-of-N on the same items at equal tokens and report effect size.

claim: Scenarios shift expert confidence differently by setting: Schoemaker 1993 (lab; 2 confidence experiments) says scenarios exploit one bias (conjunction fallacy) to offset overconfidence; Phadnis et al. 2015 (3 field experiments) found no aggregate change in confidence, only judgments moving with how an investment fares per scenario, moderated by prior confidence. Abstracts re-read this session; sample sizes unseen.
agent_test: Measure stated confidence and calibration (Brier) before and after the agent writes 2-3 contrasting scenarios, on the same items.

claim: Vivid detailed narratives can raise felt probability while lowering logical probability (conjunction fallacy), so rich scenarios risk false confidence.
agent_test: Give the agent a detail-rich vs a bare version of each scenario and check whether its stated probabilities for the rich version exceed the bare one.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Decision making after scenarios (strategy evaluation across them), not scenario creation, was the weak point: de Geus audit (via Wikipedia), Goodwin and Wright 2001 (informal evaluation can pick inferior strategies), Hodgkinson and Wright 2002 (largely failed top-team intervention). Abstracts or secondary text only.
agent_test: After drafting 2-3 scenarios force a robustness table (each candidate action scored under each scenario) and compare against choosing without it.

claim: No controlled study was found that gives an LLM the six-step Shell method and measures the result against a baseline (arXiv searches 2026-11-01: 40 and 7 hits). Closest: Polyscene (symbolic, not LLM) and practice pilots.
agent_test: This is the open test for our agent: six-step funnel vs plain prompt vs best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: Frontier LLMs ranked live Kickstarter ventures better than most humans: Spearman with outcome 0.74 (Gemini 2.5 Pro), 0.67-0.71 (GPT-5 family) vs best human 0.45, other expert 0.04, Prolific crowd 0.19; N=30 projects. Gemini minus best human 0.29 has p=0.063 (significant only at the 90% level, per the paper). Preregistered replication on 26 projects: similar pattern, lower absolute correlations, model-rank correlation across samples 0.54.
agent_test: Use pairwise ranking of candidate framings as a cheap scoring step; check it against known-outcome items.

claim: LLM forecasting is roughly at human-crowd level and below superforecasters: Halawi system Brier 0.179 vs crowd 0.149 and best plain model 0.208; 12-LLM ensemble statistically equal to 925 humans on 31 questions; Soru pipeline 0.186 vs vanilla GPT-4o 0.236 vs superforecasters 0.150; ForecastBench superforecasters 0.096 vs best LLM 0.122-0.136. Plain prompting is near chance for most models.
agent_test: Score the agent's probability outputs with Brier on resolved questions with and without scenario structure.

claim: Combining forecasters is not consistently useful: Halawi system plus crowd average beat either alone in every setting, and showing the human median raised model accuracy 17-28% (Schoenegger), but Csaszar found averaging and human-plus-LLM teams never beat the best single model (best human plus Gemini 0.67 vs Gemini 0.74; Gemini plus GPT-5 Mini 0.77, +0.03, not significant).
agent_test: Compare averaging several framings against picking the best by a pairwise rank step, at equal tokens.

claim: LLM output on open questions is homogeneous: many leading models give under 3 distinct answers in 10 queries (NoveltyBench, 20 models); same-prompt pairwise similarity usually above 0.8 and cross-model 71-82% (Infinity-Chat, 25 models, re-read this session); an LLM Delphi gave the same top themes in 12 of 12 experiments. This caps how many truly different mini-scenarios an agent gives when asked for 7 to 9.
agent_test: Count distinct framings (embedding clusters) out of 7-9 requested; test forced-distinct seeds (named drivers, sampled personas) vs plain sampling.

claim: LLM-assisted scenario workshops raise the number of scenarios but not the range of futures; drafts lean to technology fixes (80% of analysed scenarios mention technology, 61% techno-optimistic; 10 workshops, about 250 professionals, 170 drafts). Abstract only.
agent_test: Add a forced non-technology or opposite-sign driver to the funnel and measure the range of outcomes.

claim: A targeted contrasting prompt (think privately about de-escalation) beat a generic risk-balance prompt in an LLM wargame: escalation 6.37 to 2.76 (-57%) vs 4.61 (-28%); temperature 0.01 alone gave -48%. Verified in paper text. 10 runs per setting, Mistral-7B only.
agent_test: Test an explicit opposite-scenario step vs a generic balance instruction at equal tokens.

claim: Models encode story incoherence internally (linear probes 80%+, best 0.958) but their written coherence ratings barely separate coherent from incoherent stories (accuracy 0.52-0.77), so an LLM cannot be trusted to self-check scenario consistency; a symbolic planner (Polyscene) enforces consistency by construction.
agent_test: Add an external consistency check (listed constraints, second pass) to drafted scenarios and count contradictions caught.

claim: Under a symbolic diversity planner the number of distinct scenarios depends on search budget: conflicts board gave 5, 8, 9, 11 outcomes at budgets 4, 5, 6, 7 (Table 5 confirmed); unmodelled events never appear; small budgets miss outcomes needing longer event chains. The printed memory of 350 GB at budget 5 is impossible on the stated 16 GB laptop and is probably a typo.
agent_test: Vary the number of drafted mini-scenarios (3, 5, 9) and check whether late-found outcomes need longer causal chains.

claim: A small RL-trained 3B model matched large models on plausible future-news generation (48.90% vs DeepSeek-V3-671B 48.81%, Qwen2.5-3B base 47.66%), but gaps are under 2 points with no variance reported, so the gain is not shown to be real. On event-time prediction it scored 0.7780 vs 0.7503.
agent_test: Low priority: scale alone does not buy plausible scenarios, so test scaffolding over model size.

claim: On XFinBench the scenario-planning capability (246 test items, 88.6% calculation) shows a gap to experts: o1-preview 60.1, claude-3.5-sonnet 47.2, gpt-4o 46.3, Llama-3.1-8B 22.3 vs human experts 75.8; retrieved knowledge helped little on future-oriented items.
agent_test: Not the Shell method; use only as a numeric what-if benchmark.

claim: Practice pilots report large speed and cost gains with LLMs but no quality test: state-government pilot 8 vs 4 scenarios, cost down about 60%, staff hours down 60-70%; GPT-4 Time Machine reports discussion on 70%+ of scenarios (222 participants); architecture scenarios 10-15% over-engineered. Mostly abstracts or listings.
agent_test: Treat as cost evidence only; measure quality with a blind rubric.

claim: Humans using an LLM forecasting assistant forecast 24-28% more accurately than control (991 participants, six questions), even with an overconfident assistant, which suggests a draft-then-adjust pattern helps.
agent_test: Have the agent revise its answer after seeing a counter-draft and compare with no counter-draft.

claim: Business scenario planning began with Kahn at RAND in the 1950s and Wack at Shell in 1971; the 1973 oil shock gave it force; Diffenbach 1983 found alternate scenarios used by 68% of large organisations. Known only via Wikipedia and HBR landing pages, not confirmed from primary sources. Gap search 2026-11-03: HBR 1985 and 2013 landing pages (intros only) confirm Wack and Newland developed the system and that Shell dropped its UPM forecast machine in the early 1970s; the six-step recipe is still not traced to a primary text.
agent_test: None; background.

claim: The recipe step 'draft 7-9 mini-scenarios then cut to 2-3' is not found in the readable parts of Wack's 1985 HBR articles; it may be later practitioner tidy-up. Unverified because full text is paywalled.
agent_test: Treat the funnel as our own design; compare it with a plain two-scenario prompt rather than citing Wack for it.

claim: Open design questions (cut rule, diversity forcing, robustness table, optimism guard, calibration effect) have no measured LLM answer in anything reachable; they stay our own experiments.
agent_test: Equal-token arms: plain, best-of-N, funnel with max-distance cut, funnel with robustness table; measure Brier and embedding spread.
